newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela university to stamp out violent protests.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela university to stamp out violent protests.

text.p: Authorities at Venezuela's top university on Wednesday announced a crackdown on violent protests on campus, saying students who participate will be caught and handed over to police.

The decision to act against the protesters, known as "the hoods" because they cover their faces with shirts, followed a university poll on Tuesday on how to tackle the disturbances, which are almost a daily occurrence.

Venezuelan Central University rector Trino Diaz said security would be stepped up to prevent students from continuing the campaign, which often includes burning vehicles and damaging property at the university in central Caracas.

The disturbances, directed against issues such as bus fare increases, rarely lead to serious injuries but officials say they create instability. Under Venezuelan law, police are not allowed to enter universities to pursue protesters.

A group of youths, their faces hidden by shirts, rejected the decision. "We'll continue our protests because the government has to acknowledge the economic crisis which has placed us all in poverty," one told reporters.
